question: How does the conquered self stand toward opposites?
premises: Toward higher and lower selves the mind is the same.
In cold-heat, pleasure-pain, honor-dishonor it is likewise.
Abhinava: tranquil, egoless, without attraction-aversion even toward others' selves.
inference: Self-conquest is evenness toward all opposites, inner and outer.
uncertainties: K parātmasu vs vulgate paramātmanā — gloss follows K; Abhinava's prose confirms the plural reading.
plain_english: For one who has conquered the self, the tranquil — toward higher and lower selves there is same-mindedness; in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, likewise in honor and dishonor; tranquil, free of ego, with nondual mind unnegated, without attraction and aversion.
